subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Is granting `contents: read` to the fallback GitHub App installation an intentional, approved recovery boundary, and can that exact fallback path be demonstrated safely?
rationale: Repository source alone cannot establish the fallback App’s installed permissions or prove the recovery path; merging expands a credential scope on a path that standard checks have not exercised.

options.title: Prove the fallback path
options.body: Run a controlled, redacted fallback scenario that shows primary-token failure, fallback token creation, configuration read, and label application.

options.title: Approve the boundary explicitly
options.body: The GitHub App/workflow owner can confirm the fallback installation’s contents-read permission and accept the residual unexercised-path risk.

options.title: Keep the fallback least-privilege
options.body: Remove the fallback scope change and redesign configuration loading so recovery does not require repository-content access.

recommendation.title: Prove the fallback path
recommendation.body: Run a controlled, redacted fallback scenario that shows primary-token failure, fallback token creation, configuration read, and label application.

likelyOwner.reason: An App-installation or workflow owner must verify the external GitHub App permission and installation boundary.
